prize_parts.citation: for the theory of kinetic roughening of growing interfaces and its quantitative experimental confirmation as a universality class of non-equilibrium physics

statement.case_for: The Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation is the minimal, analytically transparent model of non-equilibrium growth, and its universality class turned out to be far wider than its authors could have known: exact solutions connect it to Tracy-Widom statistics and random-matrix theory, and it recurs in directed polymers, stochastic hydrodynamics and, more recently, quantum spin chains. What makes it a Nobel-type case rather than a purely theoretical one is Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments, which measured not only the exponents but the full distributions and spatial correlations and matched the exact predictions. Few results in non-equilibrium statistical physics have been confirmed this precisely. Theory dates from 1986 and the confirmation from 2010-2012, so the interpretation is stable and it has been tested across systems. After reading the other ballots I still hold that this is the strongest case from the statistical-physics side of the list, and it is the only shortlisted candidate that recognises universality and scaling in non-equilibrium systems, a direction the Committee has so far touched only through the 2021 complex-systems prize.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is mine to state against my own first choice: only one member ranked B034 at all, and the credit problem is real. Parisi was a co-author of the 1986 paper and is not credited, and the exact-solution work (Johansson, Prähofer-Spohn, Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others) that gave the field its depth is not recognised by a Kardar-Zhang-Takeuchi trio. Experimental universality is also established mainly in liquid-crystal turbulence and a few other systems, so a sceptic can say the physical reach is narrower than the mathematical reach. Compared with B042, there is no technology and no ongoing redefinition of a unit to anchor the recognition, and the committee may reasonably regard that as a lower-priority signal of lasting impact.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks (B042) are a conceptually clean invention built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, independent confirmation across several laboratories and a pending redefinition of the second; the Katori and Ye pairing is natural.
responses.response: I accept that B042 is the best-supported candidate on this shortlist and I did not rank it in my own opening, which I take as a gap in my ballot rather than a verdict. Maturity and attribution are cleaner than for my own choice. My reservation is about kind rather than quality: the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize for ion and cavity control of single quantum systems already sit next to it, so the committee should ask what new principle the lattice clock adds beyond a superb implementation. If the answer is the magic-wavelength concept with many-atom, Lamb-Dicke interrogation, I find that a fair claim, and I would be comfortable with B042 as the compromise if B034 cannot gather support.

responses.point: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B054) is a tight link between a continuum band-structure prediction and experiment, reproduced by many groups, though the origin of the superconductivity is still debated and Yuan Cao is not among the credited names.
responses.response: I ranked B054 third and we agree on the theory-experiment link; the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction before the 2018 experiments is a genuinely clean sequence. I would qualify the maturity argument more strongly than you do. A discovery of 2018 with an unresolved pairing mechanism is the kind of topic where I would want a few more years before the prize, and the omission of Cao is not a footnote but a substantive attribution problem, since the experimental breakthrough was largely his. For that reason I treat B054 as a strong later candidate rather than the right choice now.

responses.point: The Higgs observation (B026) completed the Standard Model, was independently confirmed by ATLAS and CMS, and the founding leaders Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee form a natural trio, even if credit in collaborations of thousands is hard to allocate.
responses.response: I ranked B026 seventh and not because of its science: the importance is beyond dispute. My difficulty is the statute's wording, which asks for a discovery attributable to at most three persons. Naming the founding proposers is a leadership proxy, not the people who found the signal, and your own uncertainty note concedes that spokespersons and analysis convenors could equally be argued. I would support B026 if the committee is willing to accept that proxy explicitly and defend it in the citation, but I do not think its importance by itself settles the attribution question.

responses.point: Circuit QED (B033) made strong coupling between a superconducting artificial atom and a single microwave photon routine and underlies essentially every superconducting processor; one theorist of Blais and Girvin must be left out of a four-name list.
responses.response: I ranked B033 fifth and agree on the physics and on maturity, and I think the experimental pair Wallraff and Schoelkopf is secure. I would credit Blais rather than Girvin as the theorist, since the 2004 cQED proposal was Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf and Blais led the dispersive-readout and gate theory used in the processors, but I hold this loosely: your trio with Girvin is defensible. My larger hesitation is the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, which prepared the ground and makes the committee's sense of what remains to be recognised here a matter of judgement rather than fact.

uncertainties: Whether a prize on KPZ can be framed to give fair weight to Parisi's co-authorship and the exact-solution contributors, or whether the attribution problem makes it unrecognisable as a three-person prize.
Whether B034 can attract support from members outside statistical physics, given that only I ranked it in the opening round.
How much the 2005 and 2012 prizes should count against B042 as overlapping recognition of precision-metrology and quantum-control work.
For B054, whether the unresolved superconducting mechanism and Yuan Cao's omission are still disqualifying in the near term.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: I have no documented connection to Kardar, Zhang, Takeuchi, Katori, Ye or the other credited candidates, and my work on random matrices and stochastic dynamics is subject matter rather than a personal tie, though I note that my background in that field could make me a partial rather than a neutral judge of B034.
